program.title: Bachelor of Science in Astronomy: Four-Year Curriculum Draft
program.summary: A review-ready undergraduate astronomy curriculum that begins with mathematics, physics, chemistry, computing, and sky-observation fundamentals, then advances through astrophysics, instrumentation, planetary science, cosmology, electives, and original research.

creditAudit.status: The structured JSON preserves the HTML as written; the listed semester plan currently sums to 135 credits while the program overview states a 120-credit target.

program.programArc: Years 1 and 2 establish calculus, mechanics, electromagnetism, chemistry, computation, and observational practice. Years 3 and 4 move into astrophysics, stellar and galactic astronomy, planetary science, cosmology, instrumentation, data analysis, seminars, electives, and capstone research.

degreePlan.theme: Foundations in Science, Mathematics, and the Sky

courses.title: Advanced Writing, Policy, or Society Elective

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Introduction to Astronomy with Observing Lab
courses.description: Introduces the night sky, astronomical scales, gravity, light, telescopes, the solar system, stars, galaxies, and cosmology. Laboratory work develops naked-eye observing, telescope use, sky coordinates, simple image capture, and scientific notebook practice.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: The Solar System
courses.description: Surveys planetary formation, orbital dynamics, terrestrial planets, giant planets, small bodies, planetary atmospheres, surfaces, interiors, comparative planetology, spacecraft exploration, and habitability in the solar system.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Observational Astronomy and Data Reduction
courses.description: Builds practical observing skills in photometry, spectroscopy, astrometry, image calibration, signal-to-noise estimation, and uncertainty reporting. Students reduce CCD data, analyze public survey archives, and prepare a technical observing report.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Stars, Galaxies, and the Universe
courses.description: Introduces stellar properties, stellar evolution, the interstellar medium, the Milky Way, galaxy classification, galaxy evolution, large-scale structure, dark matter, dark energy, and the observational foundations of modern cosmology.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Astrophysics I: Radiation, Matter, and Orbits
courses.description: Covers radiative processes, blackbody radiation, spectra, hydrostatic equilibrium, gravitational potentials, two-body motion, tidal effects, virial arguments, and the physical interpretation of astronomical measurements.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Planetary Science
courses.description: Examines planetary system formation, geophysics, atmospheres, climate evolution, magnetic fields, impacts, rings, satellites, exoplanet comparisons, and the chemical and physical conditions that shape planetary environments.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Astrophysics II: Stellar Structure and Evolution
courses.description: Develops the physics of stellar interiors, opacity, energy transport, nuclear burning, stellar atmospheres, main sequence evolution, late-stage evolution, compact remnants, supernovae, and nucleosynthesis.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Astronomical Instrumentation
courses.description: Studies telescope optics, detectors, filters, spectrographs, adaptive optics, calibration systems, observatory operations, space-based instruments, error budgets, and instrument proposal design.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Exoplanets and Astrobiology
courses.description: Explores exoplanet detection, demographics, orbital architectures, atmospheres, biosignatures, habitable zone models, extremophiles, prebiotic chemistry, and the scientific limits of life detection.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: The Interstellar Medium
courses.description: Covers gas and dust in galaxies, atomic and molecular clouds, emission and absorption lines, H II regions, star formation, shocks, cosmic rays, magnetic fields, and multiwavelength ISM diagnostics.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Solar Physics and Space Weather
courses.description: Introduces solar structure, magnetic activity, sunspots, flares, coronal mass ejections, the solar wind, heliophysics missions, magnetospheric response, and space weather impacts on technology.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Galactic Astronomy
courses.description: Studies the Milky Way as a galaxy, including stellar populations, kinematics, rotation curves, spiral structure, chemical evolution, dark matter, the Galactic center, and comparisons with nearby galaxies.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Cosmology
courses.description: Introduces relativistic cosmology at an undergraduate level, including expansion, redshift, distance measures, the cosmic microwave background, nucleosynthesis, structure formation, dark matter, dark energy, and observational tests.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Research Methods in Astronomy
courses.prerequisites: ASTR 210; STAT 220; junior or senior standing
courses.description: Prepares students for independent research through literature review, proposal writing, reproducible analysis, data archives, observational planning, ethical conduct, scientific visualization, and conference-style communication.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Senior Capstone in Astronomy
courses.description: Students complete an original research, instrumentation, data analysis, education, or mission-design project under faculty supervision and present written, oral, and poster-format results.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Seminar in Current Astrophysics
courses.prerequisites: Senior standing or permission of instructor
courses.description: A reading and discussion seminar on recent literature, major survey results, mission discoveries, open problems, and professional pathways in astronomy and astrophysics.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: High-Energy Astrophysics
courses.description: Examines compact objects, accretion disks, supernova remnants, pulsars, black holes, active galactic nuclei, cosmic rays, X-ray and gamma-ray instrumentation, and high-energy transient phenomena.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Radio Astronomy
courses.description: Covers radio emission mechanisms, antennas, receivers, interferometry, aperture synthesis, calibration, spectral line observations, pulsars, neutral hydrogen mapping, and radio survey analysis.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Computational Astrophysics
courses.description: Applies numerical methods to astronomical problems including N-body integration, hydrodynamics concepts, radiative transfer approximations, Monte Carlo methods, parameter estimation, and reproducible simulation workflows.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Observational Cosmology
courses.description: Focuses on cosmological measurements from galaxy surveys, supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, weak lensing, the cosmic microwave background, survey systematics, and inference of cosmological parameters.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Space Mission Design
courses.description: Introduces mission concepts, payload selection, orbital constraints, spacecraft subsystems, operations planning, risk, cost, launch environments, and science traceability matrices for astronomy and planetary missions.

courses.subject: ASTR
courses.title: Independent Research in Astronomy
courses.description: Faculty-supervised independent research in observational astronomy, theory, instrumentation, science communication, or data-intensive astrophysics. May be repeated for credit with different project scope.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus I
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Limits, derivatives, applications of differentiation, optimization, related rates, antiderivatives, the definite integral, and mathematical modeling for physical science contexts.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus II
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Integration techniques, applications of integration, sequences and series, Taylor series, polar coordinates, parametric curves, and introductory differential equations.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus III
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Vectors, multivariable functions, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, vector fields, line and surface integrals, and the theorems of Green, Gauss, and Stokes.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Equations and Linear Algebra
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: First and second order differential equations, systems of equations, matrices, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, numerical methods, Fourier ideas, and applications to oscillations, waves, and orbital models.

courses.subject: COMP
courses.title: Scientific Computing for Physical Sciences
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Introduces programming for scientific work using variables, control flow, functions, arrays, plotting, file input and output, notebooks, version control basics, and simple astronomical data examples.

courses.subject: COMP
courses.title: Scientific Programming and Numerical Methods
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Covers numerical precision, interpolation, integration, root finding, differential equation solvers, optimization, linear algebra routines, data pipelines, and reproducible computational projects.

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Statistics for Physical Scientists
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Probability, distributions, uncertainty propagation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, regression, Bayesian reasoning, model comparison, and statistics for experimental and observational measurements.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: University Physics I: Mechanics
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Calculus-based mechanics including kinematics, Newton's laws, energy, momentum, rotation, gravitation, oscillations, fluids, and laboratory measurement techniques.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: University Physics II: Electricity, Magnetism, and Waves
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Electric fields, potentials, circuits, magnetic fields, induction, Maxwell's equations in conceptual form, electromagnetic waves, geometric optics, physical optics, and laboratory applications.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Modern Physics
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Special relativity, early quantum theory, wave-particle duality, Schroedinger equation concepts, atoms, molecules, nuclei, particles, lasers, and connections to astrophysical spectra and compact objects.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Physics Laboratory
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Experimental design, measurement uncertainty, sensors, electronics, data acquisition, fitting, technical writing, and laboratory projects in mechanics, optics, electromagnetism, and modern physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Classical Mechanics
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Newtonian dynamics, central forces, oscillations, non-inertial frames, Lagrangian mechanics, coupled systems, rigid bodies, chaos, and applications to orbital and celestial dynamics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, boundary value problems, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, radiation, waveguides, and physical foundations of astronomical instrumentation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thermodynamics and Statistical Physics
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Thermodynamic laws, entropy, kinetic theory, ensembles, partition functions, blackbody radiation, phase transitions, and statistical foundations used in stellar and planetary interiors.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Atomic structure, stoichiometry, bonding, periodic trends, thermochemistry, gases, molecular geometry, and laboratory methods for quantitative chemical analysis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Chemical kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, thermodynamics, electrochemistry, solubility, coordination chemistry, and laboratory techniques relevant to planetary and astrochemical systems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic and Prebiotic Chemistry
courses.category: Mathematics, Computing, Statistics, Physics, and Chemistry
courses.description: Introduces organic structure, functional groups, reaction mechanisms, spectroscopy, carbon chemistry in planetary environments, prebiotic pathways, and chemical constraints on habitability.

courses.subject: WRIT
courses.title: Academic Writing and Research
courses.description: Develops academic reading, argument, research, revision, citation, and evidence-based writing skills with assignments that may be adapted to science and society topics.

courses.subject: GE
courses.title: Humanities or Social Science Elective
courses.description: Introduces interpretive, historical, social, or cultural inquiry outside the natural sciences. Departments may approve astronomy-relevant options such as history of science or environmental studies.

courses.subject: GE
courses.title: Arts, Culture, or Language Elective
courses.description: Broadens degree study through creative practice, cultural analysis, language learning, or comparative traditions. Students are encouraged to choose courses supporting communication across communities.

courses.subject: GE
courses.title: Ethics, Society, and Science Elective
courses.prerequisites: None unless specified by selected course
courses.description: Examines ethical reasoning and societal dimensions of scientific work, including technology, public policy, environmental responsibility, data ethics, or Indigenous and community relationships to sky knowledge.

courses.subject: GE
courses.title: Global Perspectives Elective
courses.description: Develops global and comparative understanding through history, geography, politics, culture, or environmental change, with recommended options in climate, space policy, or global science institutions.

courses.subject: GE
courses.title: Communication Intensive Elective
courses.description: Strengthens oral, written, visual, or digital communication. Recommended options include science communication, technical writing, public speaking, journalism, or data storytelling.

courses.subject: GE
courses.title: Advanced Writing, Policy, or Society Elective
courses.description: Upper-level integrative elective connecting scientific knowledge with policy, education, ethics, environment, communication, or public engagement. Suitable for students preparing capstone outreach or policy projects.

courses.subject: FREE
courses.title: Free Elective
courses.description: Open elective selected in consultation with an advisor. Recommended options include additional mathematics, computer science, geoscience, engineering, education, statistics, or approved astronomy electives.

courses.subject: FREE
courses.title: Free Elective
courses.description: Open elective supporting student goals in graduate study, teaching, public communication, data science, instrumentation, planetary science, or interdisciplinary science.

advisingNotes: Students planning graduate study in astrophysics should strongly consider PHYS 361, ASTR 474, and additional mathematics or computer science electives.
Students interested in planetary science should consider CHEM 230, ASTR 350, ASTR 478, geoscience electives, and summer field or mission-data projects.
Students interested in observational astronomy should consider ASTR 472, ASTR 476, additional statistics, and repeated ASTR 480 research credits where permitted.
The course sequence assumes calculus readiness in the first semester. Students beginning in precalculus would need a modified five-year or summer-supported plan.

reviewStatus.institutionalScope: This document is not tied to a specific institution and can be adapted to local credit, general education, laboratory, and accreditation requirements.
